notes: Read all 300 numbered source lines before editing. This is pure, non-visual computation/type code: there is NO DOM, JSX, Recharts, Leaflet, browser API, or old web UI component to adapt, so every interface (L10-76) and every computation function (L78-300) is ported verbatim with byte-for-byte identical logic, state/field names, SI unit handling (Wh/W -> kWh/kW only at the display-number boundary), and i18n key+fallback intent. Only the eight web imports (L1-L8) required native-safe handling, all documented below.

L5 `import type { ChargingSession } from '@/api/types'` -> `import type { ChargingSession } from '../../../../api/types'`, the existing native parity api/types barrel (relative depth: charging-list -> components -> charging -> features -> web-parity, then /api/types). ChargingSession there carries every field this module reads (id, started_at, ended_at, start_soc_pct, start_odometer_m/end_odometer_m, total_energy_added_wh:number, peak_power_w:number|null, cost_decimal:number|null, charger_type:string|null, cable_type:string|null, start_place:string|null), so types line up exactly.

L8 `import type { TFunction } from 'i18next'` -> local `type NativeTFunction = (key: string, fallback: string) => string`. i18next is NOT a native dependency (verified package.json), and the established native convention (e.g. YearlyTrendChart's useNativeTranslation) models the t(key, fallback) call shape used at L99-101 with exactly this signature. computeChargerBreakdown's `t: TFunction` param (L97) becomes `t: NativeTFunction`; the three t('charging.chargerTypes.supercharger'|'.dc'|'.home', 'Supercharger'|'DC Fast'|'Home / AC') calls (L99-101) keep their keys + English defaults verbatim.

L7 `convertEnergyFromSI, convertPowerFromSI` from `@/lib/unitConversion` -> inlined verbatim local ports (with their `EnergyUnitPref='Wh'|'kWh'` and `PowerUnitPref='W'|'kW'` unions): convertEnergyFromSI(wh,'kWh')=wh/1000, convertPowerFromSI(watts,'kW')=watts/1000. Used at L82 (totalEnergy), L86-89 (avgPower), L237 (spec energy), L238 (spec avgPower). No native unitConversion port exists yet, so inlining keeps this single-file conversion self-contained without re-importing the deleted/unported web path.

L2 `fmtNumber` from `@/lib/numberFormat` -> inlined local port preserving the exact web output: locale-aware fixed-precision via `new Intl.NumberFormat(locale,{minimumFractionDigits,maximumFractionDigits}).format(safeNumber(v))`, which is character-identical to the web `Number.prototype.toLocaleString(locale,opts)`; defaults match the web globals' initial values (precision 2, locale 'en-US'). The Intl.NumberFormat constructor form mirrors the proven native lib/format.ts typing. safeNumber(v) ports the web nullish/NaN->0 guard. Every call site (L111, L130, L131, L132) passes an explicit precision, so behavior is identical including the `parseFloat(fmtNumber(...))` round-trip in computeEnergyTrend/computeCostByType.

L1 `formatDateShort` from `@/lib/dateFormat` -> inlined local port: returns the universal '—' placeholder for nullish/Invalid-Date input (web FALLBACK), otherwise `new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined,{month:'short',day:'numeric'}).format(new Date(iso))` — same output as the web `toLocaleDateString(undefined,{month,day})` ('Apr 4') and same typing pattern as native lib/format.ts. Used at L110 (computeEnergyTrend date).

L3 `CHARGER_COLORS` from `@/lib/colors` -> inlined verbatim `Record<string,string>` with both the internal keys used here (supercharger #ef4444, dc #f59e0b, home #10b981 at L99-101) and the display-name keys (Home, Supercharger, 'Public DC', 'Work / L2', Other) for a faithful surface.

L4 `getChargerCategory` from `../ChargingSessionCard` (which re-exports it from `@/lib/chargingAggregation`) -> inlined verbatim, including the `ChargerCategory='home'|'supercharger'|'dc'|'unknown'` union and the exact branch order (!type->home, super|tpc->supercharger, dc|ccs|chademo|fast->dc, home|ac|wall->home, else unknown). Used at L91-93 (home/sc/dc counts), L122 (cost grouping), L269 (charger filter).

L6 `durationMinutes` from `../charging-curve/helpers` -> inlined verbatim two-arg overload `durationMinutes(startedAt:string, endedAt:string|null):number` (NOT the session-arg variant in ChargingSessionCard): 0 for missing/invalid/non-positive spans, else Math.round((end-start)/60000). Used at L84, L158, L179, L185, L192, L292.
